verdict.rationale: The MI355X is a hardware accelerator, so 'self-host' means running it on your own infrastructure rather than only renting it in a cloud. That is a fair axis, since some accelerators are cloud-only. AMD documents a self-operated deployment stack: a Customer Acceptance Guide to configure, validate and baseline the GPUs, Cluster and ROCm validation suites, a Kubernetes GPU Operator and Device Plugin, a Container Toolkit, and the Spur Slurm-compatible scheduler. All of this runs on the open-source ROCm platform, with vLLM and SGLang inference recipes. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of on-prem purchase and availability (versus cloud offerings like Azure), and independent hands-on reports of self-hosted deployments.
